text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Military ruler General Sani Abacha tells U.S. newspaper in interview that decision on whether he will contest next year's presidential election will be decided by "my own constituency", meaning the military establishment.
- Military administrator of northeastern Borno state Colonel Victor Ozodinobi sacked and replaced by another soldier in a terse statement issued by the presidency in the capital Abuja.
- Fuel supplies back to normal in Lagos area.
- Abacha tells U.S. newspaper in interview that local council polls set for last December were postponed to March this year because of bomb threats.
- Lagos state military administrator Colonel Mohammed Marwa, target of recent bomb attacks in Nigeria, insured for 10 million naira by Lasaco Assuarance Company Plc.
- A Nigerian debt fund trading some of Nigeria's dollar-denominated debt instruments to hit the local market soon; director-general of stock exchange says "it is a revolution".
